results.rationale: ts-consign-service is the root cause due to near-onset CPU and memory spikes at 1733591947, confirmed by NoiseLab inspect_noise_features with internal mechanism signals within 30 seconds. EventCausalizer assigned mechanism_strength=strong. It is observed before its callee ts-consign-price-service (onset 1733591965), and request paths exist from candidate to symptom. test_downstream_explanation confirms ts-consign-price-service's workload increase is downstream, and counterfactual_remove shows ts-consign-service observed before all symptoms. Other components (ts-contacts-service, ts-security-service, ts-user-service) are latency-only with no internal signals, as confirmed by NoiseLab compare_source_symptom. Entry component ts-admin-basic-info-service has late dominant latency, consistent with upstream propagation. Missing logs prevent exact mechanism identification, but the preponderance of evidence supports ts-consign-service.

results.rationale: ts-travel-service shows the strongest near-onset internal mechanism with a latency spike (136x latency-50, 228x latency-90) and emitter-side 503 cache exception at t=1733608978. Its log indicates it encountered a cache failure, but the emitter-side exception evidence keeps it as a root candidate. Counterfactual removal demonstrates that without its anomaly, downstream errors in ts-admin-travel-service and ts-travel2-service are prevented. ts-admin-travel-service only exhibits memory/socket at onset without error signals, and its late 500 errors align with callee failure. ts-travel2-service has lower near-onset magnitude and later cpu spike, making it a secondary effect. Other components lack propagation to the travel domain. Thus, ts-travel-service is the initiating faulty component.
uncertainties: The exact nature of the internal fault within ts-travel-service (e.g., resource exhaustion, code defect) could not be definitively confirmed.
The cache dependency mentioned in logs was not independently verified as an external root cause.
